title: Lattice slices, Ehrhart polynomials, and magic positivity of generalized parking-function polytopes
summary: For $\mathbf{b}=(b_1,\dots,b_n)\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}^n$, a $\mathbf{b}$-parking function is a sequence $(β_1,\dots,β_n)$ of positive integers whose nondecreasing rearrangement $β_1'\leβ_2'\le\cdots\leβ_n'$ satisfies $β_i'\le b_1+\cdots+b_i$. The $\mathbf{b}$-parking-function polytope $\mathfrak{X}_n(\mathbf{b})$ is the convex hull of all $\mathbf{b}$-parking functions of length $n$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that every lattice slice of $\mathfrak{X}_n(\mathbf{b})$, obtained by fixing one coordinate at an integer value, is itself a $\mathbf{b}'$-parking-function polytope of one dimension less,…
